skill.name: bitbucket-jira-cli
skill.description: Manage Bitbucket pull requests, repositories, pipelines, and Jira issues through the bj command-line interface. The skill maps familiar gh workflows to bj commands and supports branch-key automation.
skill.summary: Operate Bitbucket and Jira workflows through the bj CLI.
skill.author: spenhouet

security_audit.summary: Most backtick and device-file alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax and harmless output redirection. Unix and Windows instructions execute downloaded installers directly. The skill also directs agents to install a dependency without explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The Unix fallback pipes an unpinned remote installer directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the pipe-to-shell fallback. Use a trusted package manager with a pinned version and verified integrity after explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: The Windows installer bypasses PowerShell execution policy and executes downloaded content.
remediation.suggestion: Remove ExecutionPolicy Bypass and irm-to-iex execution. Provide a signed artifact with checksum verification and a reviewable installation command.

remediation.issue: The skill installs bj automatically when it is absent.
remediation.suggestion: Check availability, explain the package source and required changes, then obtain explicit user approval before installation.

`bj` is `gh` for Bitbucket and Jira. The command surface mirrors the GitHub CLI:
if you know `gh`, you know `bj`. It manages Bitbucket pull requests, repositories,
If a command or flag is not covered here, run `bj <command> --help`; the flags
mirror `gh` and the help is authoritative.
## Install `bj` if it is missing
Before running any `bj` command, make sure the CLI is on `PATH`. If `command -v

```powershell
Then verify, and fix `PATH` if the install dir is not picked up yet:
```bash
To run `bj` once without installing it (one-off commands, ephemeral CI), use
`uvx bitbucket-jira-cli <args>` in place of `bj <args>`. For repeated use in a
session, install it once with the snippet above so later `bj` calls just work.
Authenticate once, like `gh auth login`:
```bash
```bash
- Set `BJ_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` so `bj` never waits on a prompt; pass required
- Set `NO_COLOR=1` to drop colors and the spinner (less noise in the transcript).
- Add `--json` for the full, raw API payload; shape it with `--jq '<expr>'`
(requires the `jq` binary on `PATH`).
- Pass `--yes`/`-y` to accept confirmations (merge, close, stop).
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure (includes "not logged in"), `2` usage
## `gh` to `bj`
| `gh auth login` / `gh auth status` | `bj auth login` / `bj auth status` |
| `gh pr create` | `bj pr create` |
| `gh pr list` / `gh pr view` | `bj pr list` / `bj pr view` |
| `gh pr checkout` / `gh pr diff` | `bj pr checkout` / `bj pr diff` |
| `gh pr review` / `gh pr comment` | `bj pr review` / `bj pr comment` |
| `gh pr merge` / `gh pr close` | `bj pr merge` / `bj pr close` |
| `gh issue ...` | `bj issue ...` (Jira issues) |
| `gh repo clone` / `view` / `list` | `bj repo clone` / `view` / `list` |
| `gh run list` / `gh run view` | `bj pipeline list` / `bj pipeline view` |
| `gh api` | `bj api` |
| `gh browse` | `bj browse` |
| `gh release` | `bj release` (Jira versions) |
| `gh secret` / `gh variable` | `bj variable` (`--secured` for secrets) |
| `gh config` | `bj config` |
| `gh search` | `bj search` |
| `gh alias` | `bj alias` |
| `gh ssh-key` | `bj ssh-key` |
| `gh status` | `bj status` |
| `gh project` | `bj board` (Jira boards/sprints) |
## Differences from `gh`
- Two products behind one CLI: Bitbucket owns `pr`, `repo`, `pipeline`; Jira owns
`issue`. Each backend has its own token (`BJ_BITBUCKET_TOKEN`, `BJ_JIRA_TOKEN`).
- `bj issue` targets Jira. Issue keys look like `PROJ-42`, not numbers.
- `bj pipeline` is Bitbucket Pipelines, the analog of `gh run`.
- `--json` emits the whole raw Bitbucket/Jira response. There is no `gh`-style
field list; filter with `--jq` instead.
- `bj api` calls the Bitbucket or Jira REST API (`--backend bitbucket|jira`),
- A failed auth check exits `1` (a normal failure), where `gh` uses `4`.
`bj` reads a Jira key from the current git branch (e.g. `feature/PROJ-42-thing`
gives `PROJ-42`) and uses it automatically:
- `bj pr create` fills the PR title from the ticket, links the PR to the issue,
- `bj pr merge` transitions the linked ticket to Done after a successful merge.
Preview the effect without writing anything using `--dry-run`; skip all Jira side
effects with `--no-jira`. If no key is found, `bj` acts like a plain Bitbucket
```bash
- Run `bj pr create` / `bj pr merge` with `--dry-run` first when unsure.
- `pr merge`, `pr close`, `issue close`, and `pipeline stop` change state. In an
interactive session `bj` asks first; with `--yes` or when non-interactive it

content.user_title: Manage Bitbucket and Jira from the Terminal
content.value_statement: Bitbucket and Jira workflows often require separate tools and repeated context switching. This skill maps both services into focused bj CLI operations.
actual_capabilities: Checks bj installation and provides package-manager or one-off execution options.
Authenticates with Bitbucket and Jira interactively or through API token environment variables.
Creates, lists, reviews, comments on, merges, and closes Bitbucket pull requests.
Lists, views, creates, edits, and transitions Jira issues.
Lists repositories and runs or inspects Bitbucket pipelines.
Uses Jira keys from branch names to link pull requests and transition issues.
limitations: Requires the external bj CLI and valid Bitbucket or Jira credentials.
May install third-party software and access remote services.
State-changing commands can merge pull requests, transition issues, or run pipelines.
Raw output filtering with --jq requires jq on PATH.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Create and review Bitbucket pull requests while linking work to Jira issues from a feature branch.

use_cases.title: Manage Release Pipelines
use_cases.description: Inspect pipelines, run branch builds, and coordinate Jira status changes during release preparation.

use_cases.title: Review Team Progress
use_cases.description: List open pull requests and assigned Jira issues to review delivery status.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether bj is installed and show my Bitbucket and Jira authentication status. Do not install or authenticate without my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Open Work
prompt_templates.prompt: List my open Jira issues and open Bitbucket pull requests. Summarize priorities, reviewers, and pipeline status without changing remote state.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Linked Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pull request for branch {branch}. Use Jira key {issue_key}, preview all effects, and ask before creating anything.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Delivery Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request {pr_id}, its diff, pipeline results, and Jira issue {issue_key}. Propose actions and request confirmation before any remote change.

output_examples.input: Show my open pull requests and identify items that need attention.
output: Three open pull requests were found.
Pull request 128 needs one reviewer and has a successful pipeline.
Pull request 131 has a failed test pipeline and should be investigated first.

output_examples.input: Preview a pull request for feature/PROJ-42-validation without changing anything.
output_examples.output: Preview: create a pull request titled from PROJ-42, link the Jira issue, and transition it to In Progress. No changes were made.

output_examples.input: Summarize the latest pipeline for the main branch.
output_examples.output: The latest main pipeline failed during integration tests. The build and lint stages passed, and no retry was started.

best_practices: Use dry-run before creating or merging a pull request when Jira branch automation is active.
Confirm the workspace, repository, Jira issue, and requested state change before using non-interactive approval.
Request only necessary token scopes and avoid exposing raw API output containing sensitive fields.
anti_patterns: Do not run remote installer scripts or install packages without explicit user approval.
Do not pass automatic confirmation flags for merges, closures, pipeline stops, or Jira transitions without verified intent.
Do not print, store, or include Bitbucket and Jira tokens in prompts or outputs.

faq.question: What is bj?
faq.answer: bj is a command-line interface for Bitbucket pull requests, repositories, pipelines, and Jira issues.

faq.question: Does this skill require an MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It operates through the external bj CLI and the credentials configured for that tool.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: Use interactive login for local work or scoped Bitbucket and Jira API tokens for headless environments.

faq.question: Can it link a pull request to Jira automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. bj can extract a Jira key from the current branch and apply linked issue transitions.

faq.question: Can I use it in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. Disable prompts, supply protected credentials, and review every command that can change remote state.

faq.question: Which actions require special care?
faq.answer: Merging or closing pull requests, closing issues, changing Jira status, running pipelines, and stopping pipelines modify remote state.
